messages:
Sam: quick RFC follow-up — we need to pick a clear boundary for cost/billing tags across traces, metrics, and logs. open question: canonical storage location and propagation semantics. thoughts?
Maia: +1 we should put the canonical billing tag on the trace root (low-cardinality key) and propagate it to metrics via aggregation keys. avoid putting high-cardinality identifiers on metrics. :thinking:
Chris: how do we handle async / fire-and-forget jobs where trace context is gone? e.g., SQS, batch workers, k8s jobs.
Maia: for async we add an explicit header/field (eg `X-Redwood-Billing-ID`) and persist into job payload. ingesters can pick it up if trace isn't available.
Lee: +1 on header. propose canonical attribute names so everyone integrates consistently: `redwood.billing_id`, `redwood.cost_center`, `redwood.route`. sample snippet for trace/metric mapping:
```
// attach to span
span.set_attribute("redwood.billing_id", "team-a")
// the metrics pipeline uses redwood.billing_id as aggregation key
request_count{redwood.billing_id="team-a", redwood.route="/v1/chat"} 1
```
Chris: metrics aggregation needs that key at emit time, not just on sampled traces. if traces are sampled we can't rely on them for billing.
ingest-bot: note: trace sampling rate is 1% in prod for large services, 10% for gateways.
Maia: exactly. so we must ensure metrics emit labels or have an enrichment step in the pipeline that joins logs/headers to metrics. enrichment adds complexity/cost though.
Sam: what about cardinality? some teams want to tag by customer_id which is huge. we must forbid that on metrics but allow in logs/traces for debugging.
Lee: rule proposal: billing_id and cost_center = low-cardinality (ok on metrics). customer_id / user_id = high-cardinality -> logs/traces only and masked in any downstream aggregation unless requested and approved.
Riley (Finance): from billing side we need deterministic mapping from billing_id -> billing account. prefer a central mapping service that ingesters can query (read-only cache). finance owns the mapping.
Chris: that implies ingesters need access to that mapping service and fallback behavior if it's unavailable. caching TTL and circuit-breaker config required.
Maia: also consider private/on-prem deployments — customers might not want billing_id exported to our hosted pipelines. add config toggle to scrub or keep local-only.
Sam: good call. default: do not export billing_id outside customer VPC unless customer opts in. document in Private deployment guide.
Lee: security/PII note: billing_id may contain customer names in some orgs. we need a sanitizer stage: regex whitelist, length limit, and optional hashing (sha256) before storage.
Maia: pipeline tradeoffs: option A) emit labels at app-level on metrics (simpler, lower pipeline cost, but risk of accidental high-cardinality). Option B) minimal labels emitted, and enrichment/join in the pipeline (flexible, central control, higher cost).
Sam: which do we prefer?
Chris: prefer B for safety for multi-tenant infra, but add opt-in agent-side labels for high-throughput low-cardinality customers.
Riley (Finance): finance prefers B so we can control mapping and backfill attribution if we find late metadata.
Maia: operational tasks: 1) define canonical attribute names and allowed cardinality per attribute, 2) implement header propagation library and job payload helpers, 3) add pipeline enrichment + cache service, 4) add sanitizer + config flags for Private deployments.
Sam: owners? @Maia for schema and header lib, @Chris for ingest changes + sampling considerations, @Lee for SDK docs and sanitizer, @Riley for mapping service contract.
Maia: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up today and link to it here: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/observability-cost-tagging (WIP).
deploy-bot: deployed branch `obsv/billing-propagation` to staging — tag-prop lib v0.9 pushed. :rocket:
Chris: quick note on telemetry naming: metric label should be `redwood.billing_id` not `billing_id` to avoid collisions. include in lint checks.
Lee: agreed — add a telemetry linter rule that enforces `redwood.` prefix for our org tags.
Sam: timeline: aim for infra + header lib merged in 2 weeks, pipeline enrichment in 1 month. we'll treat metric-side label emission as opt-in for now.
Maia: I'll create action items and a follow-up doc with concrete schema and examples. ping me if you want edits before I post. :eyes:
Sam: thanks everyone. logging the action items and owners. we'll sync in next infra backlog meeting.
